facts.text: Helmville got its name from pioneer Henry Helm, who petitioned the federal government for a post office and secured the town’s name in 1872.
Helmville sits in Nevada Creek’s pastoral valley, below the Garnet Mountains, near where the creek meets the Blackfoot River, just nine miles downstream of the dam.
The Helmville Labor Day Rodeo, Montana’s biggest little rodeo, showcases bareback riders on Sunday, saddle bronc talent on Monday, and ends with a community dance.
Placer gold in Nevada Creek drew settlers, and in 1887 Washington Stapleton struck the first claims, prompting a ditch to bring water to the mines.
Before European settlement, the Kootenai, Salish, Nez Perce, Blackfeet, and Pen d’ Oreille tribes traversed Helmville’s valley.
Early Irish settlers founded Helmville, and as the town grew, families brought relatives from across Europe.
